rationale: This is a one-knob temporal re-parameterization of the archive's CashBurnFundedExternalFinance (same issuance leg, identical cash-burn gate, only 3-year summing plus winsorizing), so it is a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal and its base leg is the well-documented composite/net external financing anomaly.

The lifecycle (RE/AT) gate is a genuinely different, slower-moving conditioning variable than the archive's cash-flow gates and the sign logic is internally consistent, though both legs individually are well-trodden (issuance anomaly, RE/AT distress-lifecycle) so the incremental content rests entirely on the interaction.

The second-moment gate is an untried conditioning channel and the signed-leg/non-negative-gate construction is coherent with the stated hypothesis (stable firms shrink toward zero rather than flipping), but cash-flow volatility is strongly correlated with size and distress so the gate may end up proxying for those exposures rather than isolating "fragility amplification."

Measuring repurchases as a deviation from the firm's own five-year norm is a substantive fix for the degenerate zero-inflated leg that crippled ImprovingQualityRepurchaser, the gate direction matches the hypothesis, and the two-sided tails give a properly identified sort — main risks are the five-year history requirement eroding coverage and unwinsorized lumpy repurchase spikes.

The financing-mix (pecking-order violation) channel is a real departure from the archive's quantity-based signals, but the finding that the equity component of external financing predicts returns more negatively than the debt component is already established in the net-external-financing decomposition literature, and the expression does not actually condition on raising capital as the hypothesis claims (it relies on rank ties at zero to do so implicitly).

Sign logic is internally consistent and the non-negative two-channel SUMRANK gate is a defensible diagnosis-driven fix for the collapsed signed gate in LeverageStrainedDebtIssuance, but the base leg is just the sign-flipped net debt issuance measure from that same archive entry, so the test is closer to a re-parameterization than a new channel and will likely be highly correlated with it.
